Runtime and requirements

  • Agent budget: 2 hours
  • Compute: 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, 100 GiB storage; 0 GPU(s)

Build: 14,400 seconds. Up to 2,500 requests in two calls of at most 1,250, each allowed 10,800 seconds. No GPU; only documented external resources are permitted.

Public input and output contract

Inputs

/task/data/corpus/records.jsonl maps documents to original PDFs, extracted page text and page counts. Requests have query_id, doc_id and question; PDFs may be rendered directly. Public requests and labels are under /task/data/validation/.

Outputs

Submit executable /app/build.sh and /app/run.sh and all supporting files under /app. The fresh verifier rebuilds the index and runs commands as a non-root user with code and inputs read-only. Honor the supplied index, output, TMPDIR and cache paths; the index parent is not writable.

/app/build.sh --corpus /task/data/corpus --index-dir /work/index
/app/run.sh --index-dir /work/index --queries /path/to/queries.jsonl --output /path/to/results.jsonl

Return query_id, an answer string and supporting 1-based pages. Give the final answer and units directly; say when information is absent, using an empty page list when no evidence exists.

The index remains writable across repeated query calls.

Evaluation

MMLongBench-Doc integer and float answers use the source answer-extraction prompt and numeric comparators. Text, list and unanswerable answers use a binary semantic judgment of the question, reference and full submitted answer. Equivalent wording receives credit; incorrect entities or comparisons, missing list items and unsupported claims do not. Each semantic judgment records a reason. FinRAGBench-V retains its original binary answer judge. Trusted model calls use google/gemini-2.5-flash through OpenRouter.

Average answers within each source, then give the two sources equal weight.

Evidence-page precision, recall and F1 are diagnostics, not part of the primary answer score. Out-of-range source page references are excluded only from citation diagnostics and do not remove the corresponding answer question.

Reward mapping

The final reward uses the raw quality described above, with fixed reference quality b = 0.4350989780543772 and integer score anchor a = 20 on the 0–100 scale:

reward(q) = (a / 100) * q / b                             if 0 <= q <= b
            a / 100 + (1 - a / 100) * (q - b) / (1 - b)  if b < q <= 1

This maps raw quality 0, b and 1 to rewards 0, a / 100 and 1. Raw quality and auxiliary diagnostics are reported separately. Harbor retains the 0–1 reward precision; a displayed 0–100 score is rounded to one decimal place. Correctness and trajectory-audit gates take precedence over this conversion.

Validity and failure handling

The verifier checks execution, output structure, document/page validity and stage limits. Completed valid rows survive query-call timeout; missing or invalid rows receive zero. Other query-command failures invalidate that call. Trusted answer-extraction or judge transport failures invalidate the measurement rather than establishing a low baseline or model score.

Final reward requires a healthy, accepting independent trajectory and submission integrity audit. Audit failures are reported separately from retrieval quality and cannot produce positive credit.
